_readme: Third-party skill decisions for tsdevstack. `install[]` = blessed, auto-installed by init/sync via `npx skills add <source> --skill <skill> ...` pinned to `ref` (not re-hosted). `candidates[]` = vetted but not yet enabled. `rejected[]` = considered and declined, with reason (kept for the record).

install.name: Next.js dev-loop (official — Vercel / Next.js core)
install.note: Version-agnostic: verify runtime behavior after editing app code. Pinned by SHA (no stable tag carries it yet).

candidates.name: Next.js Cache Components (official) — revisit later
candidates.note: Enable if/when the generated frontend adopts Cache Components on Next 16.3+. Not applicable at 16.2.6.

rejected.name: NestJS (third-party)
rejected.reason: Models already know NestJS basics. tsdevstack's value is its custom layer (nest-common wrappers, modules, guards, decorators). Authoring an in-house nest-common skill instead of blessing a community NestJS skill.

rejected.name: Kong (Kong/ai-marketplace, official)
rejected.reason: Skews to Kong Konnect (SaaS) / decK workflows. tsdevstack generates and deploys kong.yml itself. Covered by the in-house add-an-endpoint / gateway skill instead.
